findings.issue: The iOS pinned commit was duplicated verbatim as a checkout ref in both CI workflows with nothing binding those copies to spec/topic-only.lock.json, which TOPIC_ONLY_MIGRATION_MATRIX forbids by name after six measured drifts. Mutating both refs left preflight, the document check and the topic gate suite all at rc=0. The only test that read those workflows asserted fetch-depth, the preflight command and the pytest list, never the ref value.
findings.disposition: Each named iOS checkout block is now extracted per workflow and its ref bound to lock.pinned_commit.ios, so a drift in either copy or in both fails the gate that both CI workflows already run. Mutating the real workflow files now returns rc=1 in all three cases against a green baseline. Three synthetic drift controls cover tests-only, docs-only and both. Those controls call the helper directly, so deleting the wiring from the real-file gate left every one of them green — measured — and an AST trip-wire now requires the gate to call the helper exactly once with both workflow texts and the lock-read pin. Battery scripts/mutation_c3_ios_pin_gate.py: 8 of 8 killed, none survived, none invalid. The thirteenth copy, IOS_SHA in tests/test_topic_only_ledger.py, is deliberately left unbound: it is a real-commit fixture for validator tests, the same category as SERVER_SHA in that file, which is not the server pin either — binding it to the lock would make it wrong.

findings.issue: The SEM-037 gate shipped with a battery that reintroduced the duplication it exists to forbid. scripts/mutation_c3_ios_pin_gate.py hardcoded the iOS pin, so c9b3572 carried fourteen copies while the SEM-037 disposition described IOS_SHA as the thirteenth and only deliberate exception — the disposition was momentarily untrue as written. The battery's drift value was also a fixed literal, so a pin that happened to equal it would have turned the three real-file mutants into no-ops reported as SURVIVED, making the battery fail without exercising the intended mutations. The 896e46d follow-up commit message repeated this with the opposite verdict, claiming those no-ops would still be reported as KILLED.
findings.disposition: The battery now reads the pin from spec/topic-only.lock.json and derives the drift value from it so the two can never coincide; the repository is back to thirteen copies and the SEM-037 disposition is true as written. Re-run: eight of eight killed, none survived, none invalid, restore hashes identical. A per-file occurrence check was also added to the both-drift mutant, but it is currently unreachable: the three drift controls already assert exactly one occurrence per workflow file, so a duplicate makes the baseline red and the battery aborts before any mutant runs — measured by appending a second copy to tests.yml, which produced rc=2 with no mutant lines. It is redundant safety, not an exercised branch. The pushed 896e46d message remains immutable history; this journal correction records the actual no-op classification as SURVIVED rather than rewriting published history.

findings.issue: The S1a′ C2 re-baseline first scoped its locator re-derivation to the six gated documents plus the hash chain, which is the same gate-outside blind spot SEM-034 recorded. Three separate errors followed from treating the shift as a uniform mechanical rewrite. A blanket regular expression moved app/main.py:2718 inside the SEM-035 finding text, even though an earlier C2 commit had explicitly frozen that coordinate as a record of a past defect, and the baseline tree already showed it pointing at build_period_exchange_series rather than the cache store it narrates. The implementation ledger kept the superseded manifest hash because the re-derivation walked the claim ledger and the semantic review but not that file. A repository-wide scan then found twenty-one candidate coordinates past the changed hunk rather than the eight the reviewer had reported, and the reviewer confirmed its own list was an omission reached by tracing only the three documents named in SEM-034 rather than by classifying every candidate.
findings.disposition: Every candidate was classified by comparing what the surrounding prose claims against what the cited range actually contains in the old pinned tree, rather than by trusting either list. Eight unique live locators matched their prose and were advanced, giving eleven occurrences once markdown label and anchor forms are counted separately, on top of the thirty-three occurrences inside the hash chain and the gated documents. Seven unique locators were already inconsistent with their prose at the old pin, so they are not drift produced by this C1; re-sealing them at the new pin would preserve a wrong target while falsely signalling that this change had corrected them, and they are therefore left untouched and separated as pre-existing debt for a follow-up C4 that must re-audit the sibling coordinates of the same claim clusters as well. This finding closes the misclassification and the scope claim, not those seven citations, and this verdict asserts nothing about their present accuracy. The SEM-035 coordinate was restored and re-frozen, and the implementation ledger was rebound to the current manifest. A repository-wide live versus historical locator gate, which would require an explicit marking convention such as the full forty-character blob form already used in finding locations, is deliberately deferred to its own slice rather than widened into this re-baseline. This finding text itself now carries the same frozen coordinate a second time, so it is subject to the identical rule: a later re-baseline must not advance app/main.py:2718 here either, and that duplication is itself part of the argument for the deferred marking convention. A second re-baseline then remapped four more coordinates, seven occurrences, inside this journal's own finding narratives, which is the same error the frozen SEM-035 coordinate already warned about. The rule is therefore not a per-coordinate exclusion list but a class rule, and it separates three kinds rather than two. Locator tokens under .findings[*].issue and .findings[*].disposition are immutable journal text: changing one requires an explicit semantic amendment, never an offset remap. A locator explicitly bound to a commit or blob SHA is likewise historical. A locator already inconsistent with its prose at the old pin is not thereby historical — it is unresolved pre-existing debt and must stay unchanged pending a semantic audit, which is also why this verdict asserts nothing about its present accuracy. Everything else is only a live candidate and still requires old-versus-new target verification before it moves.

findings.issue: The LOAD-S5 C2 re-baseline rewrote the R-HAND-4 bullet to describe the new single-flight budget and cancellation semantics, and in doing so dropped the only current-state cue the claim carried. The candidate extractor requires a code symbol, a current-state cue and an assertive ending together, so the rewritten sentence fell out of the claim candidate set even though it is still a present-tense assertion about the very code that commit had changed and still carries its own file-and-line provenance. The claim ledger shrank from sixty-five entries to sixty-four and the code-fact count from fifty-four to fifty-three, and nothing failed. This journal records a reverse audit of assertions outside the candidate set, but that flag is a stored judgement rather than an executed check, and the re-baseline refreshed its hashes without re-performing it, so the compensating control did not observe the loss either. The reproduction is exact: removing the cue again and regenerating the ledger and this journal the way a re-baseline does leaves all two hundred and six existing document gates green.
findings.disposition: The cue was restored so the assertion is a claim candidate again, and the code-fact entry it lost was reinstated and re-verified against the pinned tree, returning the ledger to sixty-five entries with fifty-four code facts and eleven normative units. A pinned inventory of candidate and classification counts was added alongside the existing locator inventory, and under the reproduction above it is the only check that fails. That inventory does not make the candidate set complete and the conservative-lint limitation stands unchanged; it makes a shrinking review surface require a human edit with a dated reason instead of passing silently, and it does not detect an equal-sized substitution of one candidate for another. The restored bullet also gained a third locator, because its two existing ones showed the budget definition and the shared wrapper but not the worker binding that installs the checkpoint, so the checkpoint clause was true but unsubstantiated by its own provenance. Two reciprocal work units were added to the edge list so the verdict covers them: the opposite participant's review of the LOAD-S5 implementation commit, bounded to what was actually examined and explicitly excluding a byte-level re-derivation of that round's thirteen moved coordinates, and this author's follow-up together with the review that demanded these edges. reviewed_at was advanced to 2026-08-20 accordingly.

residual_limits: Natural-language completeness and citation entailment are not mechanically provable. This pass covers only the work units explicitly listed in review_process.review_edges; later changes must reopen the verdict and obtain a new opposite-participant review edge. The boundary is the edge list itself, not a finding number, because a hand-written endpoint goes stale on the next round.
Negative repository facts use full-tree searches at the pinned commits and must be rerun if either pinned commit changes.
The documents remain Draft implementation contracts. This pass confirms the cited C1 code path at the pinned commit, not operating activation or completion of R-GATE-1.

This hash-bound semantic review does not establish mutable production state. Commit 5f9aa74 reports a separate read-only observation at 2026-08-12 13:09 UTC, but its raw command, host/container identity, and output are not preserved in the reviewed inputs; activation still requires a fresh direct measurement.
The 2026-08-12 historical amendment before ADR-041 is outside the document hash used by this journal and remains a separately reviewed, non-hash-bound note.
Release arming remains excluded from the frozen baseline and requires a separate explicit GO.
The initial-snapshot lease gate authorizes the start of send_json, not its completion; an in-flight send may finish after the lease expires.
A post-ACK snapshot skip is fail-closed but produces no removal, reauthorization, or close notification, so a client can be told a topic was accepted and then receive no initial data.

The shared lease gate performs an O(number of subscribers) scan and set allocation per topic. This is accepted for the current scale and supported-topic bound, not established as a large-scale guarantee.

Citation existence has two syntax gates: backtick-form `path:N[-M]` locators inside manifest-owned RID blocks plus the full baseline are checked at the lock pin, and Markdown `#L` links across the full text of the six canonical documents are checked at the lock pin or an explicit same-repository 40-character commit. Both gates check only path existence, bounds, and limited label/anchor agreement; neither proves that the target entails the surrounding prose. Backtick locators in non-RID prose outside the baseline, unlinked prose line numbers, and semantic drift can still survive a green re-baseline (SEM-012/SEM-023/SEM-024).

In the final stage, every authenticated subscribe containing at least one authorizable topic makes one cache-free RevenueCat HTTP round trip: the WS authorization path calls fetch_revenuecat_result directly and the stale-cache fallback exists only in the REST helper. This availability and latency coupling is unmitigated and gates activation.
FX enforcement is bounded by the unauthenticated legacy broadcast until Stage B. This slice closes the topic contract, not the service-wide paywall (R-OPEN-4).
The working tree was edited concurrently by two agents during this review. The reported verification is pinned to one tree hash rather than a continuous observation of a frozen tree.

This token-bearing C2's procedural drift inventory found 27 changed locator occurrences in five source documents and 24 changed occurrences in the derived claim ledger, for 51 total. This count excludes unchanged citations and is not comparable to historical C2 counts unless the same extractor, base, and scope are rerun. RID-contained backtick locators and full-document Markdown links now receive mechanical existence and bounds checks, but correctness of moved claims still rests on exact-tree semantic review.

Re-baselining verifies that citations point at existing code, not that the surrounding prose is still true. SEM-018 shows the two can diverge while every gate passes; only reading each cited passage against the new behaviour closes it, and that step is procedural.

The forbidden-phrase check that keeps the code default from being promoted to an operational fact has no exemption for a measured statement: once production is actually sampled, the same forbidden substring still trips even if source and timestamp are appended. A measured result must use distinct wording such as '2026-08-12 direct measurement found WS_TOPIC_AUTH_STAGE=compatibility' and include its source and timestamp. This is a deliberate cost of phrase matching; adding semantic exemptions would make the check itself a guess.

The stage matrix binds the documented aggregate columns to the planners, but its subject is the R-INV-2 table alone. Prose elsewhere in the same documents can still contradict the code without any gate noticing; SEM-018 was found by reading, not by a check.

The anonymous rollout counters contain request and connection-event counts but no traffic-provenance label. A zero immediately after restart establishes the observation interval only; it cannot prove that later events were organic rather than manual or synthetic probes. Nonzero counters therefore establish matching request events, not nonzero organic traffic or end-user transition impact.

Journal closure terminates when the author prepares the complete fixed/pass candidate first and the opposite participant reviews that exact tree without modifying it. Committing the unchanged tree adds no unreviewed file content; any post-review tree edit invalidates the attestation and requires another review. globally_independent_reviewer=false limits independence of the artifact as a whole, but does not make reciprocal review of an exact final tree impossible.

The unverified_token_bearing counters run before Firebase verification and store fixed-cardinality request and connection-event counts only. They do not establish valid-token demand, authenticated users, or actual RevenueCat calls. final_stage_rc_candidate is conditional on the injected topic-availability snapshot and later dispatcher, stage, and token gates; process restart resets every counter.

SEM-024 repairs the three known Markdown-link locator debts outside ADR-041, adds a full-canonical-document #L gate, and validates all baseline backtick locators against the pins. SEM-025 removes the backtick extractor's extension allowlist and checks it against an independently expressed locator-shape oracle. Those checks cannot discover plain prose line numbers without a recognized locator and cannot prove semantic entailment; historical code claims therefore use immutable full-SHA blobs, while target meaning still requires review.

The one-branch-at-a-time audit that measured 32 of 40 errors.append sites as neutralisable (33 before SEM-026) is closed by SEM-029: every site now fails a control that names its own diagnostic, re-measured on this tree as 40 sites, 0 invalid, 40 red, 0 survivors. Coverage is of append sites, not of rule variants — a single site inside a loop serves many participant fields, scope flags and finding keys, and those variants remain unaudited.

Commit messages, annotated tags, deployment reports, terminal transcripts, and agent memory are outside this journal's hash-bound inputs unless a review edge explicitly identifies and preserves the exact artifact. In particular, a562391's unpreserved 46-connection observation is not promoted to activation evidence; 9f0aec9 corrects only its invalid client-absence inference.

SEM-028 pins the currently reviewed extraction surfaces: seven Markdown-literal test modules, nine semantic-drift inputs, 125 RID backtick locators, and six canonical Markdown-link documents. These inventories prevent silent shrinkage but do not prove that heuristic discovery is complete, that dynamically assembled paths are visible, or that a locator semantically entails its prose; legitimate additions and removals require reviewing and updating the corresponding inventory.

The semantic input binding chain begins at a genesis fingerprint of this journal as it stood when the binding was introduced. Genesis fixes a baseline; it does not assert that every work unit landed before it passed through a review edge. The edge list at genesis names the LOAD-S5 implementation and its re-baseline, but other work that landed between the S1b REST auth lane isolation and genesis is named nowhere in it — among it the account deletion sweep, the snapshot Redis I/O bounds, the snapshot request deadline with worker checkpoints, the deploy verifier and runbook gates, the KRX expiry holiday correction, the PostgreSQL service and workload profile work, the M0a maintenance installer, and the mutation harness isolation. That enumeration is not exhaustive and no total is asserted, because this journal has no canonical rule for grouping commits into work units. Residual limit one already places whatever is unnamed outside what this pass covers, and the binding constrains transitions after genesis rather than the ones that preceded it. The binding also fixes bytes rather than judgement: an epoch is a reciprocal record, not evidence that a person re-read the work. Each epoch after genesis must carry at least one prose work unit in some direction, so a transition cannot pass as a fingerprint receipt alone. Requiring one in both directions was rejected: a work unit belongs to a single author-reviewer edge, and forcing the opposite direction would invite an invented entry.

R-CLI-24 is implemented at pinned iOS commit 45a8a12, and the 45-second LOAD-S4 multi-client rehearsal completed using the server cooldown and client jitter candidates. This pass does not establish a count hard cap for either admission waiters or same-key followers, and it does not perform permanent activation. Two non-blocking iOS test gaps also remain: abnormal reconnectDelayNanoseconds inputs and a superseded 30-second stability task.

Server C1 4849992 narrows the WebSocket proxy to exact `location = /ws`, so suffix and trailing-slash paths do not inherit Upgrade headers or 600-second timeouts. It adds no `limit_req` or `limit_conn`: R-DEC-4 and R-LOAD-2 still require a handshake `limit_req`, while the per-IP connection cap remains measurement-dependent. This epoch does not choose an uncalibrated rate or claim that the confirmed ingress requirement is complete.

This C2 pass was authored by Claude Code and cross-reviewed by OpenAI Codex, which returned NO-GO. Three of its findings landed as iOS 1de20ea (degrade predicate parity, retry-scheduling fail-open, ordinary-refresh releasing the server premium latch) and two stale-prose findings were corrected here: R-HAND-6 still asserted the server does not close on publish send failure, and R-CLI-11 still asserted no banner renders in MODE 2 — both were the opposite of the pinned code. Claude Code's own adversarial subagent rounds (49 findings with 12 surviving; then 20 with 4 surviving) preceded that review and are not a substitute for it: they missed both stale-prose items, and the locator round had flagged R-HAND-6 without it reaching the repair list.

The /ws handshake limit was implemented by OpenAI Codex and re-baselined by Claude Code. Codex's own C2 plan named pin, ledger and hash re-binding but did not enumerate the three prose assertions its C1 falsified — baseline E4, R-LOAD-2's body, and the FREE_TIER open item — which is the same failure mode Codex had caught in the preceding R-GATE-3 pass, now in the opposite direction. The rate itself (10r/s, burst 20) is a provisional capacity guard, not a measurement: there is no v2 subscriber traffic to derive it from, and handshake rate only proxies auth load because authorization happens on subscribe, not on the upgrade. Re-evaluate from phased lrs= observation. IP-level limit_conn stays deferred under R-DEC-4 (3).

The R-GATE-3 family is now recorded as done, not verified: the evidence is the implementer's own commits and tests, and R-CLI-16's once-per-generation forced reconnect still has no mutation coverage. Separately, this pass records a deployment gap that provenance alone does not expose — server commit 4b58110 (fresh_premium / premium_active / R-HAND-6 close-on-send-failure) is committed, pushed and pinned but the production app image predates it, so the runtime OpenAPI exposes neither the query parameter nor the response field. Only the nginx layer was deployed. Flag ON must not precede deploying that server code with topics off.

Two items this pass corrected were overstatements in the prior GO-risk list, not new defects: reauth exhaustion no longer stops silently (hard-expiry forces one reconnect per generation), and the cold-start snapshot fan-out is four calls total, five with KRX entitlement, not four per topic. The remaining B8 caveat is narrower than before: the reactivation path is now locked by transport-level regression, but automated coverage still speaks only to code recovery — operational flag flips and the auth/UI integration remain the device smoke's responsibility. R-CLI-16's once-per-generation reconnect invariant still has no mutation coverage.

R-CLI-16's once-per-generation reconnect invariant now has mutation coverage (two topics expiring in one lease generation; moving reconnect into the per-topic loop fails 2 != 1), superseding the prior pass's residual. Two process limits remain visible from this pass. First, the citation gate checks only that a cited line exists inside the file, so inserting lines mid-file silently redirects every citation below it — C2 943581e advanced the iOS pin without re-deriving locators and twelve citations pointed at unrelated code until this pass. Second, an audit of all 118 iOS citations at the new pin found twelve whose range begins one to three lines before the cited declaration; these predate this cycle and still contain the cited content, so they are recorded rather than churned.

The production deployment gap recorded two passes earlier is closed as of the 2026-08-21 12:57 KST direct runtime check. The running app container started at 2026-08-21T01:21:02Z; its app/main.py and app/topic_initial_snapshot.py SHA-256 values exactly match production checkout ed7b2eb, which contains server C1 4b58110. Runtime OpenAPI exposes the fresh_premium query parameter and the EntitlementsResponse premium_active field, while topic_flag.py still reports OFF with no pending operation or lock. Deploying 4b58110 is therefore no longer an activation prerequisite; this observation does not itself approve flag ON.

Release GO was recorded on 2026-08-21 accepting three risks for the initial phased release: no per-IP limit_conn, the server-side stale registry cost of expired leases, and in-connection subscribe abuse that nginx cannot see. The GO is a decision only — this cycle changed neither the server flags nor the iOS Release arming, both of which remain off, and server flag ON requires a separate approval under R-GATE-4. The /ws 10r/s + burst 20 re-evaluation is deliberately not one of the accepted risks: it is a phased-release observation duty, and any value change is a host config change requiring its own approval.
